doc.title: Bob Schulz interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

chapter: Jazz parties and life in Wisconsin
title: Teaching music for seventeen years and leaving for San Francisco
summary: He taught grades one to twelve, married in 1963, honeymooned in New Orleans, divorced, and moved to San Francisco to join Turk Murphy.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, kind of a well-rounded bunch of things to do, in education and performing. Did you teach elementary up to high school, or the whole thing?

Yeah. I started out teaching everything from first grade through twelfth grade, because it was very small schools, and then I was in junior high and then I ended up for the last eleven years just teaching in high school. The typical, you know, marching band, jazz ensembles, solos and ensembles, concerts, that kind of thing.
Well did you give that up to play more?

Well I gave it up not on purpose, I probably would have still been teaching if it wouldn’t have been for the fact that I got divorced. I got married in ‘63, which was kind of interesting because my wife and I at that time went to New Orleans on our honeymoon, © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

and I saw Jack Teagarden just before he died, because he died I think in January of ‘64, And a bunch of other musicians down there, it was great. But she was not that crazy about the music. She liked the music but I was gone a lot. And it didn’t mix. So we parted our ways. I have three great kids from there that have grown up, two girls and a boy, and then I came out and joined a gentleman by the name of Turk Murphy in San Francisco. So I moved away, I quit teaching, I asked for a sabbatical but they wouldn’t give it to me because teaching jobs were hard to get, at least music teaching. So I moved out to San Francisco and started playing out there. And re-married and have a twelve year old boy right now.
So San Francisco is your home now?
Yes. Well I shouldn’t say, it’s the area. I live in Marin County, I live in San Anselmo which is about fifteen miles away.
Did you have the gig before you moved.

I had the gig but it was also iffy. If you cut it you got the gig. I mean if I didn’t cut it I would have been out. So then I would have probably moved back to Wisconsin. I couldn’t have taught where I was, but I would have gone somewhere else.
